observation_summary: The compiler fails to correctly detect inheritance when a prototype is directly assigned, leading to 'JSC_UNKNOWN_OVERRIDE' warnings. The test failure shows that 'this' references are incorrectly resolved to 'null' instead of the expected type.
hypothesis: The compiler's type inference and prototype handling logic failed to correctly propagate type information when prototype inheritance was established via direct assignment. The fix involves ensuring that 'this' references are correctly typed during devirtualization and that the 'FunctionType' correctly identifies 'prototype' as a property.
prediction: The code would show missing type propagation for 'this' references and an incomplete implementation of property checking for 'prototype' in 'FunctionType'.
experiment_rationale: The fix modifies 'DevirtualizePrototypeMethods' to explicitly set the JSType on the new name node and updates 'FunctionType' to correctly handle 'prototype' in 'hasOwnProperty' and 'setPrototype' logic. These are procedural corrections to how the compiler handles type information and property resolution.
reasoning_summary: The bug is an incorrect implementation of the type inference and devirtualization logic. It is not a missing check (Checking), nor a simple value assignment (Assignment/Initialization), nor a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object). It is a procedural error in how the compiler processes prototype inheritance and type propagation, which fits the definition of Algorithm/Method.
evidence_used: The fix modifies 'DevirtualizePrototypeMethods' to set JSType on a new node.
The fix modifies 'FunctionType' to add 'hasOwnProperty' logic and update 'setPrototype' logic.
The failing test shows 'this' references resolving to 'null' instead of the expected type.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves associations between prototype and function types, the root cause is the procedural failure to correctly compute/propagate these types during the compiler pass.
